planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; this cultivar's genuinely dwarf stature makes it one of the few mulberries that performs well in a large patio pot.

directions: The result of a multi-decade dwarfing breeding project by Japanese grower Hajime Matsunaga, this selection stays in the 5-to-7-foot range at maturity, far smaller than ordinary mulberry trees, while remaining self-fertile and precocious. Its most useful trait is fruiting on both old and new wood, which stretches the harvest window across several months instead of one short flush. It is sold in the UK nursery trade under the name Charlotte Russe, where it won Chelsea Flower Show Plant of the Year honors, but is the same Morus rotundiloba selection marketed in North America as Mojo Berry. Give it full sun and evenly moist, well-drained soil, and expect fruiting within a year or two of planting.
